title: Daily Devotional #9
paragraphs: As I read through Matthew chapter 9, I am struck by the power and compassion of Jesus. He healed the sick, forgave sins, and called sinners to repentance. He showed us what it truly means to be a servant of God, by reaching out to those in need and demonstrating your love in practical ways.

In verses 2-7, we see how Jesus heals a paralyzed man. He not only healed the man physically, but also forgave his sins. This reminds me that you are not only concerned with our physical well-being, but also our spiritual well-being. You desire to forgive us of our sins and make us whole.

In verses 9-13, we see how Jesus calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow him. Jesus did not come for the righteous, but for sinners. This is a reminder that no matter how far we have strayed from you, you are always willing to accept us back into your loving arms. Your grace is sufficient for us, and you are always willing to forgive us when we come to you with a contrite heart.

In verses 18-26, we see how Jesus heals a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years, and raises a young girl from the dead. These miracles show us that nothing is impossible for you. You have the power to heal us physically, emotionally, and spiritually. We need only to come to you in faith, trusting in your goodness and mercy.

Finally, in verses 35-38, we see how Jesus had compassion on the crowds, who were like sheep without a shepherd. He encouraged his disciples to pray for more workers to go out into the harvest field. This is a reminder that we are called to be your hands and feet in this world, to bring hope and healing to those who are hurting. We need to pray for more workers to join us in this mission, and to be willing to step out in faith and serve wherever you call us.

Lord, thank you for the example of Jesus in Matthew chapter 9. Help us to follow his example of compassion and service, and to trust in your power and goodness. May we be your ambassadors in this world, bringing hope and healing to those who are in need. Amen.
